name: Almroth Wright
summary: British bacteriologist and immunologist who pioneered typhoid vaccination and opsonic therapy.

name: Leonard Colebrook
summary: British bacteriologist and author of the biographical lecture on Wright.

name: Trinity College, Dublin
summary: University in Dublin where Wright graduated in medicine.

name: Army Medical Services
summary: British military medical organization where Wright served as Professor of Pathology.

name: Royal Victoria Hospital, Netley
summary: Military hospital in Netley where Wright established his laboratory headquarters.

name: St. Mary's Hospital
summary: London hospital where Wright worked as Professor of Pathology and Bacteriology after 1902.

name: British Army
summary: Military force in which Wright conducted typhoid inoculation trials.

name: War Office
summary: British government department responsible for the Army, which initially opposed Wright's trials.

name: United States Army
summary: American military force that conducted parallel typhoid inoculation trials.

name: Alexander Fleming
summary: Bacteriologist and assistant to Wright who later discovered penicillin.

name: John Freeman
summary: Assistant to Wright who worked on opsonic indices and typhoid data.

name: Douglas
summary: Assistant to Wright who worked on opsonic indices at St. Mary's.

name: W. B. Leishman
summary: Wright's successor at Netley who produced statistical data on typhoid vaccine in 1909.

name: Louis Pasteur
summary: French microbiologist whose work on anthrax and rabies influenced Wright.

name: Robert Koch
summary: German physician who discovered the tubercle bacillus and influenced bacteriology.

name: Typhoid Vaccine
summary: Vaccine developed by Wright to protect soldiers against typhoid fever.

name: Opsonic Factor
summary: Substance in serum discovered by Wright that makes microbes acceptable to leucocytes.

name: Capillary Pipette
summary: Laboratory tool devised by Wright for bacteriological methods and blood testing.

name: Wright's Capsule
summary: Device devised by Wright for collecting small samples of blood.

name: Spreader
summary: Tool devised by Wright for spreading blood films to study leucocytes.

name: Lymph Leech
summary: Contrivance devised by Wright for exerting gentle suction on wound walls to collect lymph.

name: British Medical Journal
summary: Medical journal that published Colebrook's lecture on Wright in 1953.

name: Netley
summary: Location of the Royal Victoria Hospital in England.

name: South Africa
summary: Location of the war where typhoid fever caused heavy losses.

name: France
summary: Country where Wright set up a laboratory for wound infection study during WWI.
